- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast slightly to align with upward momentum.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model overpredicts; reduce forecast to reflect downward pressure.
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +10%+ in 3-5 days), especially when sentiment is mixed or neutral — apply a 1-2 day lag correction downward.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is 5%+ above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1-3% unless sentiment strongly supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates late-period rallies (last 7-10 days of forecast) — adjust upward by 1-2% if sentiment turns bullish in final 3-5 days.
- If sentiment swings sharply (e.g., from 0.33 to 1.00 in 2-3 days), model lags in reaction — adjust forecast 1-2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
